AI features arrive (video summaries and LinkedIn writing help), playback controls reach videos embedded on other sites, and every Netflix extra becomes opt-in. New: AI features. A new AI Features tab lets you summarize videos and get LinkedIn writing help. Use a small daily allowance after you sign in, bring your own OpenAI or Anthropic key, or run a local model. Every AI feature falls back to the built-in generators when AI is not available. New: controls for embedded videos. Floating controls, keyboard shortcuts and right-click actions now work on videos embedded in other websites, like YouTube or Vimeo players inside articles and courses. The extension loads into an embedded frame only when it contains a video. Improved: Netflix features are opt-in. Netflix extras are off by default, and you turn on the ones you want in Settings, on the Netflix Features tab. Existing setups were reset once. That way everyone starts from the same place. Improved: accurate Netflix watch-time and limits. Watch-time tracking and viewing limits now count only while a video is playing in a visible tab, so a background tab does not use up your daily limit. Fixed: per-site pause stays on this device. The list of sites you paused the extension on no longer syncs across devices.

The team's other apps get a permanent home in Settings, and the promotional panel comes off the top of every Settings page, so only one banner can sit above your settings. New: "More from the developer" tab. Settings has a new tab that collects the team's other apps in one place, with a logo, a short description and a link for each. Until now the list appeared only as one step of the welcome page, so skipping setup meant losing it. The list is bundled with the extension, and nothing is fetched to show it. Opening a product is not tracked. New: "More apps" in the popup. A link at the bottom of the popup opens that tab directly. Improved: a calmer Settings page. The promotional panel that sat above every Settings page moved into the new tab, so Settings opens to your settings. A banner that does appear there stands down while the "finish your setup" reminder is showing, so two are never stacked. Improved: clearer store listings. The Chrome, Edge and Firefox listings now describe which parts of the extension link to the team's other apps, and the Chrome "contains ads" question is answered: self-promotion only, with no ad network, ad SDK or tracking involved.

When the extension clears Netflix's "device isn't part of the Netflix Household" screen, Netflix hides its own player controls, so keyboard controls now take over in that case. Every keyboard shortcut can be changed. A key can belong to only one shortcut, and your shortcuts follow you when you are signed in. New: Netflix recovery controls. After the extension clears the Household screen, Netflix keeps its player controls hidden. Only then, keyboard controls switch on: Space to play or pause, ← / → for 10 seconds, Shift + ← / Shift + → for 1 minute, Ctrl + ← / Ctrl + → for 5 minutes, Ctrl + 0 to Ctrl + 9 to jump to the start or 10% to 90%, Ctrl + - to jump to 1 minute before the end, V for subtitles, B for the audio track, plus volume, mute and fullscreen. A small notice on the player tells you they are on and links to the full list. New: change any shortcut, one key per action. Every shortcut, including the new Netflix ones, can be given another key in Settings, on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab. If the key you pick already belongs to another shortcut, you are told which one, with a link that takes you to it. New: shortcuts follow you when signed in. Your key bindings are saved in this browser and, while you are signed in, to your account, so another device picks them up the next time you open Settings on it. Fixed: announcements that never appeared. Four places where the Video Controls Plus team can post announcements (the Settings banner, the popup card, the one-time card and the opt-in notification) were showing nothing. They work now. Each one reads at most 20 entries.

Netflix and LinkedIn menu actions now run at once, and Settings shows only the switches and shortcuts that do something. The website and the store descriptions were corrected to list only what the extension does today. Improved: Netflix and LinkedIn actions run straight away. Opening a panel, starting a timer, exporting or downloading from the widget or the right-click menu now happens immediately. Before, most of these only switched the feature on and asked you to reload the page. On/off switches still apply after a reload. Fixed: four LinkedIn tools that did nothing. Profile Backup, Message Export, Job Tracker and Job Alerts had a switch and a menu item and never ran. Each now performs its action from the menu. Response Tracker and Message Scheduler had no working part and were removed. Improved: Settings that only show what works. The New Features page listed 127 switches, and only five of them changed anything. It now shows those five (gesture controls, VR / 360 mode, SponsorBlock, ad accelerator, scroll-wheel volume) with the scroll-wheel options. The Netflix switches are in the Netflix section, as before. Improved: keyboard shortcuts that all do something. 64 shortcut entries that had no effect were removed from Settings. That frees their keys. The mini-mode key and the Player Overlay display option also did nothing and are gone, and the shortcut group that was titled "v10 Features" is now called Bookmarks. Ctrl + Alt + F now opens and closes the filters tab, and Ctrl + Alt + O adds a bookmark at the current moment. New: info button on two more LinkedIn panels. The post performance overlay and the quick preview card now carry the same info button as the other panels, and it explains what the panel is and how to use it. Improved: descriptions that match the extension. The website, its license catalog and the store listings named tools that are not in the extension yet. They now list only what you can use today, with the real shortcut keys and the features that need a sign-in.

Your account now lives on our website, and the extension connects to it on Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Everyone connects once after this update. An account that existed before 16.0.0 opens empty until we finish moving the old cloud data, which follows this release. Nothing saved in your browser is affected. New: connect the extension to your account. There is no sign-in inside the extension any more. Press Connect to your account, and a tab opens on vcpeai.aoneahsan.com. Sign in there with Google, check that the page and the extension show the same short code, and press Connect this browser. The code lasts 10 minutes. You do this once in each browser, and Sign out in the extension disconnects that browser only. New: accounts on Firefox. The same steps work on Firefox, where there was no working sign-in before. New: one switch for usage analytics. Settings → Privacy & Data has a Usage analytics switch. It is on by default, and it works with or without an account. Switch it off and the extension stops sending usage events, stops counting which sites, features and speeds you use, and stops the location lookup. Crash reports to Sentry have their own switch beside it, Third-Party Error Tracking. Improved: Delete All Data deletes the account. In 15.3.0 the button removed your stored files, your profile, your synced settings and your usage data, and it left your notes, your watch-later items and the account itself. It now deletes the account, the files stored under it and everything saved under it. Improved: the shared AI allowance is counted on our server. A connected account gets 3 runs a day on our key. With your own OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a local model, there is no limit from us and you do not need an account. The extension also no longer asks your browser for the identity permission. Fixed: removing a synced watch-later item. In 15.3.0, removing a video from watch later did not remove it from your account once it had synced. Removing a video, or moving it up or down the list, now works on synced items.

You can now say a note instead of typing it: on a video in the extension, and on the website and in the Android app, where Speak also fills flashcards, a report or a feature request. Every AI run now has a level, Spark, Pulse or Surge, and a new Plans page shows what each plan gives. New: Speak a note on a video. On the widget's Tools tab, press "Speak a note", record up to 2 minutes, then check the note and save it. It's pinned where the video was when you started. The first time, a tab opens so you can allow the microphone once. You can switch Speak off in Settings → AI Features. New: Speak on the website and in the Android app. Press Speak on Notes, Flashcards, Contact or Feature requests and say it instead of typing. You see what was heard and what it became. You decide what is kept. The Android app asks for the microphone only when you first press record. New: AI levels: Spark, Pulse and Surge. Every AI run now has a level. It sets how much reasoning goes into the run, and your plan decides the level you get. The Plans page lists the level each plan gets, and the popup's AI Video Summary card and Settings on the website show your level and today's runs. New: a Plans page. The new Plans page lists Free, Pro and Team, paid monthly or yearly. Every feature is on every plan, and Pro and Team raise the daily AI runs and the AI level. Choosing a plan opens the Contact page, and the Video Controls Plus team sets it up. Improved: an AI pause says until when. On Free, when AI rests for a while, the card says "AI is resting until …" with the time. Your runs are untouched. Everything else works as usual. On Pro and Team, AI keeps working all day. Improved: recordings are deleted within 24 hours. A Speak recording, its transcripts and the proposal are deleted within 24 hours, or at once when you press Discard. A recording that becomes a proposal uses 1 AI run, and a silent recording or a failed upload uses none. The Privacy Policy has the details.

The widget does a lot more now: comfort for your eyes and captions, study tools, your library, looks and zoom, voices and rooms, GIFs and clips, automatic playback, and watch parties. It also carries 16.1.0 and 16.2.0. New: comfort for your eyes and captions. Comfort (View tab) warms the picture, makes colors clearer, restyles a site's own captions and adds a reading guide. It needs no account and sends nothing. New: study tools beside the video. A Study timer runs focus rounds and breaks. On videos with captions, "Show transcript" lists them beside it and "Make chapters with AI" turns them into chapters for 1 AI run. New: your library from the video. Connected, the Tools tab adds "Quiz at this moment", "Save a word", "Diary entry", "Learning path", "Collection" and "Search your library". Wiktionary looks up a saved word. It gets only the word. New: looks, effects and zoom. Filters → "Looks & overlays" adds 20 color grades, four art looks, "Sharpen" and "Blur a region". "Zoom & fit" (View tab) needs no account. Some sites block filters on protected video. New: voices and rooms that keep the speed. The Audio tab adds balance, five voices, four rooms, "Even loudness" and a limiter. They skip protected video. New: GIFs and clips made on your device. Tools → "Capture & export" makes GIFs, clips, time-lapses, screenshot bursts and contact sheets, and "Annotate" marks screenshots. They skip protected video. New: playback that runs on its own. Playback → "Automation" blocks autoplay, keeps a per-site speed, ramps speed and sets reminders, and Settings adds "Watch limits" and "One video at a time". New: share & watch together. "Share this moment" gives a link and QR code. Watch together keeps play, pause, seeking and speed in step for up to 20 people. Everyone needs a connected account. Fixed: auto-skip presses the skip buttons. The Settings auto-skip switches did nothing; now they press Netflix's and Prime Video's own Skip Intro, Skip Recap and next-episode buttons after your 0–2 s delay. They need a connected account. Fixed: Netflix runs its own controls. Before, Netflix pages ran the ones for X. Improved: a Docs link. Settings and the popup link the docs site. Fixed: your language at once. Spanish, French and German screens show their language from the start.

Seven website pages now have a short tour you start from the header, and a new How it works page walks through Video Controls Plus in six steps. The extension itself is unchanged. New: page tours. documents.t: Video Controls Plus began as "Udemy Video Playback Speed Controls", a speed control for one site, and the Video Controls Plus team builds and maintains it. Today it ships for Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

It's a browser extension. You set the speed, loop a part, and change the sound and the picture of the video on the page you are watching, from the keyboard or the widget. It works on YouTube, Netflix, LinkedIn, Udemy, Vimeo, and any other site with a standard video, and it has extra tools on YouTube, Netflix and LinkedIn.

The Video Controls Plus team writes the extension, these docs and the release notes. What changed in each release is in the changelog. The docs describe what the extension does today, and a control that needs an account says so on its page.
Use the contact page on the website. Tell us which site, which browser and which key, and we can find the problem faster.

There is no sign-in inside the extension. You create your account on vcpeai.aoneahsan.com, where you sign in with Google, and then you connect the extension to it. Connecting works the same way on Chrome, Edge and Firefox. An account that existed before 16.0.0 opens empty until we finish moving the old cloud data, which follows this release. Nothing saved in your browser is affected.

Press Connect to your account. The button is in the popup, on the account step of the welcome page and on the Account & Sync tab in Settings. A tab opens on vcpeai.aoneahsan.com. If the page asks you to sign in, press Continue with Google. Check that the page and the extension show the same code. If the codes are different, press Cancel. Press Connect this browser. The extension shows the connection within a few seconds while the popup or Settings stays open, and otherwise within about 30 seconds. The code lasts 10 minutes. If you closed the tab, press Open the page again in the extension. Troubleshooting covers what to do when connecting fails.

Connected, the extension stores your account data and your settings, and while the Usage analytics switch is on it records which sites, features and speeds you used. The full list is in Privacy and permissions.

Connect the extension to your account. Open the Account & Sync tab in Settings and turn on Enable Cloud Sync. Your settings are uploaded when you turn it on. Your speeds, key bindings and site settings are synced. The tab shows the last sync time. Bookmarks saved while connected sync to your account separately from this settings switch; bookmarks made while signed out remain in that browser. Button What it does Upload to Cloud Saves the settings on this device to your account Load from Cloud Replaces the settings on this device with the copy in your account Newer settings win: when two browsers save to the same account, the account keeps the newer copy. Settings you changed on this device and did not upload are overwritten by Load from Cloud. Another device picks up your keyboard shortcuts the next time you open Settings on it, but the list of sites you paused does not sync. It stays on the device where you paused them.

Sign out, in the popup or on the Account & Sync tab, disconnects this browser only. Your account stays, and so does every other browser you connected. To connect this browser again, press Connect to your account.

Open Settings, go to the Privacy & Data tab, and click Delete All Data on the Your Data card. It deletes the account itself, the files stored under it and everything saved under it. It cannot be undone. The button needs a connected account, because it deletes what is stored with your account. Export My Data is on the same card. It downloads your data as a JSON file. It also needs a connected account. You can also delete your account from the website's data deletion page when you are signed in there.

documents.t: Open the Data Management tab in Settings. Export Settings downloads your settings as a JSON file. You choose whether to include video memory and filter presets. Import Settings restores from a file you exported: Replace All replaces your current settings, and Merge keeps your current values where the file has none.

Every feature works on Free. Pro raises your daily AI runs and your AI level, for one person, and Team does the same for each member. The prices are on Plans. To get Pro, sign in on the website, open Plans and press Upgrade to Pro, monthly or yearly. You pay on Polar's checkout page, and Pro starts on your account as soon as Polar confirms the payment. Polar emails you a link to its customer portal, where you can cancel, change your card and download invoices. Cancel any time. Your plan runs to the end of the period you paid for. Team is set up with us: press Choose Team on Plans, which opens the contact page. Plans are bought on the website only, never inside the extension or the Android app. For anything else about your account, use the contact page.

Video Controls Plus has three AI features: a summary of a YouTube video made from its captions, writing help on LinkedIn, and Speak, which turns what you say into a note. Each runs only when you start it. Your own key or a local model needs no account, and the Shared allowance and Speak need a connected account. Open the popup on a YouTube watch page and press Summarize this video. Writing help starts on LinkedIn (LinkedIn page). Every playback control works without AI.

documents.t: Pick one on the AI provider card, in Settings → AI Features. Option on the card What you need Where your text goes Shared allowance A connected account To the Video Controls Plus server, which sends it to Anthropic. On Pro or Team only, when that route is unavailable, it goes to OpenAI instead. Your OpenAI key or Your Anthropic key Your API key, no account Straight from your browser to that provider Local (Ollama) Ollama on your machine Nowhere. It stays on your device. A summary, a LinkedIn writing-help answer or a Speak proposal uses 1 of your plan's daily runs on the Shared allowance, and the popup's AI card shows how many you've used today. Each plan's daily runs and its AI level (Spark, Pulse or Surge) are on Plans. On Free, AI sometimes pauses. The card says "AI is resting until …", your runs are untouched, and everything else works. On Pro and Team the run goes to a second provider instead, and your own key and a local model have no limit from the team.

Say it, then check what was written before anything is saved. Speak is in three places: The extension: Speak a note on the widget's Tools tab, on any video. It pins the note at that moment of the video. The website: Notes, Flashcards, Contact and Feature requests. The Android app: the same four pages. A recording is up to 2 minutes. The first time, the extension opens a page, "Allow the microphone for Speak", to ask once. A recording where nothing was heard, or that failed to upload, uses no run. Speak works on the Shared allowance only.

Feature What is sent Video summary The caption or transcript text of the video LinkedIn writing help The text you are drafting Speak Your recording, to our server, which sends the audio for a transcript and then only the transcripts to the AI (see Three ways to run it) While you record, your browser's own speech recognition may also send your voice to your browser's maker. The video itself is never sent.

Your recording, its transcripts and the proposal are deleted within 24 hours, or at once when you press Discard, and if our file storage cannot be reached at that moment, the audio file is removed at the next hourly check. For a summary or writing help, the team does not store the text you send or the answer. For each Shared allowance run, the server keeps a usage record for 13 months, without your text, and a count of today's runs. A key you add stays in your browser and goes only to its provider. Without AI, a summary falls back to the extension's built-in generator, with no model. The microphone and everything else are on Privacy and permissions.

Video Controls Plus keeps your settings in your browser. While the Usage analytics switch is on, and it is on by default, usage events are sent to the team's backend with or without an account, and your IP address goes to ipapi.co for a location lookup at most once a day. A connected account also stores your account data and, with sync on, your settings. Turn the switch off and none of the usage recording happens. It does not record the videos you watch, their titles or their addresses, unless you turn on Watch History, which is off by default. Saved items are the other exception. A connected account keeps a video's title and address only with something you save to it or start from it: a note, a bookmark or diary entry, a watch-later item, an uploaded screenshot, extracted video details, a transcript, a flashcard saved from a video, a learning-path video, a collection item or a watch party. This page is a plain reading of the privacy policy. The policy is the legal text. Where the two differ, the policy is the one that counts.

Your settings, your keyboard shortcuts, the speed remembered for each video, your playback position, your filter presets and your audio settings are stored in your browser. They go to your account only when you connect the extension and turn sync on. Audio download is processed on your device. A screenshot stays on your device unless you choose a cloud action for it, which uploads the image. Watch limits count minutes on this device only, and their PIN is hashed and never synced. The Study timer's counts and the chapters made from a video's captions stay in this browser. GIFs, clips, time-lapses and contact sheets are made on your device and saved as downloads.

Data When What it is Usage events While Usage analytics is on, with or without an account The event name, the site's hostname, your browser, your operating system, the extension version and a session id, plus your account when the extension is connected Location lookup While Usage analytics is on, at most once a day Your IP address is sent to ipapi.co. The country, city and timezone it returns are saved to your profile when an account is connected; the region stays in your browser. The IP address is not stored. Sites, features and speeds While Usage analytics is on, with a connected account Which sites, features and speeds you used Account With a connected account Email address, display name, profile photo and your Google account id This browser With a connected account A device name, the browser, the operating system, the extension version and when it was last seen Settings With a connected account and sync on Your settings, synced to your account What you save to your account With a connected account, each only when you save it Notes, bookmarks, watch-later items, uploaded screenshots, extracted video details (the right-click extract action) and transcripts you save to the account, each with the video's title and address. A bookmark also saves its timestamp, and a diary entry is a bookmark that also holds a mood and your words. Flashcards saved from a video (a quiz moment, or a word with the caption line on screen as its example), learning-path videos and collection items are kept the same way. Watch History Only after you turn on Watch History in Settings, on the Privacy & Data tab, and play a video while connected. It is off by default for each connected account on each browser. For each viewing session of 15 seconds or more: the video's title and address, the watch time, the last position, the parts of the video you played, the date, the playback speed and the features you used. Turning the switch off stops new sessions from being recorded. What is already there stays in your account until you delete it on the website or delete your account. Watch parties When you start or join a watch party The video's address and title, the party code, and who joined and when. While the party runs, play, pause, a jump to a new time and the speed are passed to its members through Supabase Realtime and are not stored. Error reports While Third-Party Error Tracking is on Crash reports sent to Sentry AI text Only when you start an AI feature The captions of the video, or the text you are drafting. A usage record for each Shared allowance run is kept for 13 months, without the text. See AI features. Speak recordings Only when you record with Speak Your voice, up to 2 minutes, with its transcripts and the proposed note. All three are deleted within 24 hours, or at once when you press Discard (privacy policy, 1.8). In usage events a site is its hostname, such as youtube.com. Full addresses, page paths and page titles are not part of an event.

Open Settings, go to the Privacy & Data tab, and find Usage analytics. It works with and without an account. Off, it stops three things: Usage events are not sent to the team's backend. A connected account does not record which sites, features and speeds you used. Your IP address does not go to ipapi.co. If the switch is off in this browser or in your account at the moment you connect, it ends up off in both.

They are on the same tab. Switch Default What it controls Third-Party Error Tracking On Crash reports to Sentry Marketing Communications Off One thing: an occasional browser notification about new features or another product from the team. Email is separate: product news reaches account holders, each email with a one-click unsubscribe link. Settings Sync On Storing your settings with your account Third-Party Error Tracking is separate from Usage analytics, so turning one off does not turn off the other. Under Your Data on the same tab you can export or delete your data, and Account and sync has the steps.

Service What it holds Supabase The database and the sign-in for your account, and the live sync of a watch party FilesHub Stored screenshots, Speak recordings for up to 24 hours, and the email the team sends Sentry Crash reports, while Third-Party Error Tracking is on ipapi.co Receives your IP address for the location lookup, while Usage analytics is on Anthropic, OpenAI and Groq The text of an AI run you start, and the audio or transcripts of a Speak recording. AI features says which one gets what. Five features contact a service of their own, each only while you use the feature: SponsorBlock (sponsor.ajay.app), Netflix subtitle translation or dual subtitles (api.mymemory.translated.net), Netflix ratings with your own key (www.omdbapi.com), an AI summary that has to fetch a video's captions (video.google.com/timedtext), and Look up in the widget's Save a word (en.wiktionary.org), which receives only the one word you typed. The policy's section 5.9 lists one more service, for a feature these docs do not cover yet.

The policy lists these as not collected: the videos you watch (unless you turn on Watch History), video content or media files apart from a screenshot you choose to upload, your browsing on pages where the extension does nothing, passwords, payment information, and the content of pages you visit apart from text you send to an AI feature yourself and what the five features above send to their own services. Your data is not sold.

Speak is the only feature that uploads your voice, and the microphone is asked for the first time you use it. Where What you see The extension Speak a note shows "Allow the microphone once". Press Open the microphone page, and a tab called "Allow the microphone for Speak" opens. Press Allow microphone, then choose Allow in your browser's own box. You do this once. The Android app The app asks for the microphone permission when you first press record in Speak. The Firefox add-on Firefox also asks for its optional "Personal communications" data permission before anything is recorded or sent. The microphone is on only while you record. If you block it, the page tells you where to switch it back on. Turn Speak off in Settings, on the AI Features tab, and the extension stops offering it.

The extension asks for seven permissions and for access to sites, and on Chrome and Edge for an eighth, offscreen. It does not ask for the identity permission, because there is no sign-in inside the extension. The microphone is not a permission it asks for at install. Permission Why the extension asks for it storage Saves your settings, shortcuts, speed memory, filter presets and theme in the browser activeTab Lets the popup read and change the video in the tab you are on when you open it contextMenus Adds the right-click menu items alarms Timers for the sleep timer, sending queued sync and usage batches, checking a pending account connection, refreshing remote switches, lifting a per-site pause when it ends, and one daily check for an announcement notification. notifications Shows speed changes, loop status and sleep timer alerts when the widget is hidden or the display mode is Notification Only clipboardWrite Copies a link to your clipboard from the right-click items "Copy Page URL" and "Copy URL with Timestamp"; the clipboard is never read scripting Brings the controls to a video embedded inside another page, and only into a frame that contains a video offscreen (Chrome and Edge) Lets Speak record in a hidden page of the extension and send the recording from there, so the recording keeps going while the upload runs. Firefox records in its background page and does not need it. Access to all sites Finds and controls the video on any site you open Access to all sites is the broad one. The extension needs it because a video can be on any site. While a site is paused, the extension does nothing there.

Firefox asks for three optional data permissions, and each one gates what is sent. Firefox permission What it gates Technical and interaction data Usage events are sent only if it is allowed. The Usage analytics switch asks for it. Website content Page content (a screenshot you upload, a transcript you save to the account, captions for an AI run, a word you save with its caption line) is sent only after you allow it. The add-on asks the first time you use one of those. Personal communications A Speak recording and its transcripts are sent only after you allow it. The add-on asks the first time you use Speak.

An A-B loop replays the stretch between two points you set. Looping needs an account. Speed control does not. If the loop keys do nothing, connect an account first.
documents.s: Loop a part of a video with an A-B loop

documents.t: Play the video to where the hard part starts. Press Ctrl + Alt + A. That is point A. Let it play to where the part ends. Press Ctrl + Alt + B. That is point B. The video jumps back to A when it reaches B, and it plays that part until you clear it. You can also set A and B with one click each on the widget's Loop tab. It helps with a guitar lesson that has one fast bar, a lecture where the proof goes by in 40 seconds, and a language video with one sentence you can't catch: set A and B around the part, slow the speed with [, and it plays until you have it.
Key What it does Ctrl + Alt + A Set the start point (A) Ctrl + Alt + B Set the end point (B) Ctrl + Alt + L Turn the loop on or off Ctrl + Alt + Backspace Clear both points

You pick the mode on the widget's Loop tab, and the widget's labels are in English (why). Mode What happens at B Forever The part repeats until you turn the loop off Once The part repeats one time Times The part repeats the number of times you set, from 1 to 20 With Times, a progress indicator shows how far through the repeats you are, and the count stops at 20, so for more, use Forever and turn it off yourself with Ctrl + Alt + L.
, and . step back and forward one frame, which helps you put A and B on the exact spot. Every key is in Default shortcuts, and you can change them in Change a shortcut. Next: Audio boost.
Audio boost raises the volume beyond 100%, up to 400%, after you connect an account. Press Ctrl + Alt + U to raise the boost and Ctrl + Alt + Y to lower it.
Key What it does Ctrl + Alt + U Boost up by 20% Ctrl + Alt + Y Boost down by 20% Ctrl + Alt + N Normalize on or off The same controls are on the widget's Audio tab.

A quiet recording, such as a lecture recorded from the back of a room, stays quiet at the player's 100%, and boost takes the volume past that limit, between 100% and 400%. Each press moves it by 20%. At 400% a loud video is very loud, so raise it a little at a time.

Normalize reduces the dynamic range: the gap between the loudest and the quietest parts gets smaller. Turn it on with Ctrl + Alt + N for a video where the speaker whispers and the intro music does not.

The extension remembers the volume and the mute state per site. Set YouTube quiet and a course site loud, and each one comes back the way you left it. The Remember Volume card is in Settings, on the Video Features tab.

It does a lot more with the sound than make it louder: bass boost, noise reduction, vocal isolation and five more are each one button under Advanced Audio on the widget's Audio tab. The tab needs an account, so you reach them after connecting one. Button What it does Bass Bass boost Denoise Noise reduction, which filters background noise Spatial Spatial audio Vocals Vocal isolation Compress The audio compressor Karaoke Karaoke mode Pitch The pitch preset EQ Equalizer presets
Audio download saves the audio of a video as WebM or WAV. It does not save MP3. Its switch is Audio Download, in Settings on the Download & Capture tab, and the audio is processed on your device.
The three audio keys are part of the full table in Default shortcuts, and each can be moved in Change a shortcut. The picture is next: Video filters.

Audio tools change the balance, the voice, the room and the loudness of the video you are watching, and they sit on the widget's Audio tab, which needs a connected account like the rest of that tab. They change only what you hear on the page. They do not work on protected video, such as Netflix and Disney+. The widget says so.
documents.s: Change the balance, voice, room and loudness

documents.t: Control What it does Left / right Moves the sound toward the left or the right speaker; Centre is the middle Mono Plays both channels as one Swap L/R Swaps the left and right channels

Pick a Voice: Chipmunk, Deep, Robot, Echo or Telephone. Each one is a real pitch shift, and the video speed never changes. The Pitch button under Advanced Audio is the Deep voice. Pick a Room: Small room, Hall, Cathedral or Cave. Room mix sets how much of the room you hear. Off under either one puts it back.

Even loudness brings quiet parts up and loud parts down, by at most 12 dB. Turn it on for a video where the speaker is soft and the music is not. Limiter stops the sound from going past a Ceiling you set, from -1 dB to -12 dB. It keeps a sudden loud moment in check. Turn audio tools off switches all of them off at once.

Settings, Video Features tab, Audio tools holds the same controls: Balance (left / right), Mono, Swap left and right, Voice, Room, Room mix, Even loudness, Limiter and Limiter ceiling. Reset audio tools puts them back.

The widget shows one of three messages: Message What it means "Not available on protected video (Netflix, Disney+ and similar): its audio cannot be processed." The site protects the video, and the audio cannot be changed "Not available on this video: the site does not let its audio be processed." The video comes from another site that does not allow it "Starts when the video plays." Press play and the tools start Audio boost and normalize are separate controls on the same tab, with their own keys and their own page, which also covers the eight Advanced Audio buttons.
Two optional shortcuts start with no key: "Turn audio tools on or off" and "Swap left and right". Each needs a connected account. Give one a key in Change a shortcut. Next: Capture and export.

Auto-skip clicks the skip button for you when Netflix, Prime Video or YouTube shows one. The skip switches are off until you turn them on, and all of them need an account. Account and sync covers what connecting adds.
documents.s: Skip intros, recaps and credits automatically

documents.t: Site What it clicks Netflix and Prime Video The skip button for an intro, the skip button for a recap, and the "Next Episode" prompt over the end credits YouTube The "Skip Ad" button, and the next video on the end screen It clicks the buttons the site shows. If the site shows no button, there is nothing to click.

Open Settings and go to the Advanced tab. Find Playback Features. Turn on the ones you want. Switch Default What it does Auto Skip Intro Off Clicks the intro skip button Auto Skip Outro/Next Episode Off Clicks through the end credits and the "Next Episode" prompt Auto Skip Recap Off Clicks the recap skip button on Netflix and Prime Video Show Skip Notification On Shows a short notice each time it skips

Skip Delay is how long the extension waits after the button appears, and 2 seconds is the longest. Option What it does Instant (0ms) Skips with no wait Fast (250ms) Waits 250ms Normal (500ms) Waits 500ms. This is the default. Slow (1s) Waits 1 second Very slow (2s) Waits 2 seconds Pick a slower delay if you like to see the button before it goes.
Press Ctrl + Alt + S to skip the intro yourself, or click Skip Intro on the widget's Smart tab; the key works on Netflix and Prime Video only.

Control What it skips Where Silence Skip The silent parts of a video Widget, Smart tab, Silence Skip SponsorBlock Sponsor segments Settings, New Features tab, which needs an account Silence Skip works without an account.
Ctrl + Alt + S is the only skip key. Its row is in Default shortcuts, and Change a shortcut moves it. Next: Display and widget.

Capture & export makes a GIF, a clip, a time-lapse, a burst of screenshots or a contact sheet from the video, and it lets you draw on a screenshot. Open the widget's Tools tab and find Capture & export. It needs a connected account, like the screenshot. Everything is made on your device and saved as a download. Nothing is uploaded.
documents.s: Make GIFs, clips, time-lapses and contact sheets

documents.t: Button What you get GIF · next 5 s A looping GIF of the next 3, 5, 10 or 15 seconds, 320, 480 or 640 px wide ● Record clip A clip with picture and sound, as WebM. Press ■ Stop clip to end it Time-lapse 4x The video at 2x, 4x, 8x or 16x, picture only, as WebM Burst every 5 s A screenshot every 2, 5, 10 or 30 seconds while the video plays, up to 100 Contact sheet 3×3 3 × 3 or 4 × 4 frames from across the whole video, each with its time, as one PNG Annotate A screenshot you draw on The numbers on the buttons follow your choices in Settings. A clip and a time-lapse stop by themselves after 10 minutes, or when the video ends. When a burst is on, the button shows how many shots it has. Save them with Save … as ZIP (the button shows the count), which gives a ZIP of PNGs, or Save as sheet, which puts them on one image.

Press Annotate. The Annotate screenshot panel opens on the current frame. Pick a tool: Arrow, Box, Highlight, Text or Pen. Pick a color: Red, Yellow, Green, Blue or White. Drag on the picture to draw. With Text, click, type, then press Enter. Press Save PNG to download it, or Copy to put it on the clipboard. Ctrl + Z undoes the last mark. Escape closes the panel.

Settings, Video Features tab, Capture & export sets the GIF length, the GIF width, the Time-lapse speed, how often a burst fires (Burst every) and the Contact sheet size. Reset capture settings puts the defaults back.

Protected video, such as Netflix and Disney+, cannot be captured, and some other sites do not allow their frames to be saved. The widget tells you which it is. A contact sheet needs a video with a known length, so it does not work on a live stream. A paused video cannot be captured, so press play first.

Three optional shortcuts start with no key: "Record or stop a clip", "Make a GIF" and "Annotate a screenshot". Each needs a connected account. Set them up in Change a shortcut. To share a clip shaped for social posts, see Share and watch together. Next: Playback automation.

Comfort warms the picture, makes colors easier to tell apart, restyles the captions a site already shows, and adds a reading guide over the video. Open it on the widget's View tab, under Comfort. It needs no account. Your Comfort choices are stored with your other settings, synced to your account only when cloud sync is on, and nothing is sent anywhere.
documents.s: Make videos easier on your eyes with Comfort

documents.t: Where What you find Widget, View tab, Comfort Quick switches for the four tools, and More comfort settings Settings, Video Features tab, Comfort & accessibility Every option, and Reset comfort settings Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts, Comfort Four shortcuts that start with no key

Turn on Eye comfort and move Warmth (0% to 100%) for evening watching. Only the video changes, never the page. Tick Also lower brightness to soften it more. Turn on by itself between set times switches it on and off on its own. Set From and Until, and it starts at 21:00 and ends at 07:00 until you change them.

Pick a Type: Green-weak, Red-weak, Blue-yellow or No colour. Then pick a Mode: Make colours clearer shifts colors so they are easier to tell apart. Show how it looks shows the video the way someone with that color vision sees it.

Caption style restyles the captions the site already shows, on YouTube, Netflix, Prime Video, Udemy, Coursera, Vimeo, Khan Academy, Video.js players and videos with WebVTT tracks. It does not create captions. Choose a Caption look and a Text size. Look What it is Default White text on a dark band High contrast Larger bold white text on solid black Dark Soft light text on dark gray Minimal Smaller text on a lighter band Large print Large bold yellow text Colourful Bold green text on deep purple Easy reading A plain sans-serif with wider letter and word spacing and taller lines, dark text on cream

A soft band holds your eyes on one line of captions or on-screen text. Pick a Shape (Band, Line or Spotlight), then choose Stay put to keep it at one height on the video or Follow the pointer to have it move wherever your mouse goes. Height on the video sets where it sits. Strength sets how strong it is.
Comfort works with Video filters and the cinema colors at the same time. They stack. The extension combines them into one filter on the video, so turning on one does not turn off another.

The four Comfort shortcuts start with no key: "Toggle eye comfort", "Toggle colour vision", "Toggle caption style" and "Toggle reading guide". They are optional. Give one a key in Settings, as Change a shortcut shows. Next: Visual effects and zoom.
You choose how the controls appear on the page in Settings, on the General tab under Display Mode. It works without an account.
documents.s: Choose how the controls appear on the page

documents.t: Mode What you see on the page Floating Widget The widget, a control panel you can drag anywhere on the page. This is the default. Notification Only A small speed indicator when the speed changes, and no panel The widget's Tools tab has the same choice under Display & Theme, where the two modes are labeled Floating and Notify. Notification Only suits you when you drive everything from the keyboard, you already know your keys, and you want nothing sitting on top of the page while the video plays.

These are on the General tab, under the display mode. Setting Choices Widget Position Top Left, Top Right, Bottom Left, Bottom Right Widget Size Normal, Compact, Minimal Open Widget On Click, Hover Out of the box the widget is Normal size and opens on a click.
Press Esc or Ctrl + Alt + H to hide the widget, and press again to show it. To switch the whole extension off on one site, use Pause per site.

Open the Appearance tab in Settings. Option How many Color schemes 20 Font families 11 Border radius options 6 Font size scales 5 There is also a compact mode and a reduced motion switch. The 11 fonts come with the extension, and none of them is loaded from a remote font service.

Settings and the popup are available in English, Spanish, French and German: Auto-detect Language follows your browser's language, and Language lets you pick one yourself. The widget is in English today. It stays in English when Settings is in Spanish, French or German.

Key What it does Esc Hide or show the widget Ctrl + Alt + H Hide or show the widget \ Show the current speed The starting keys are listed in Default shortcuts, and Change a shortcut shows how to move them.

Connect your account before saving a note. Each note keeps the video timestamp and appears on the website's Notes page. The widget's Tools tab has the note editor, export buttons and a library chooser.
documents.s: Take notes and add bookmarks while you watch

documents.t: Open the widget and go to the Tools tab. Under Notes & Extraction, click Note. Type the note in the prompt and confirm. The note is queued with the current timestamp for your account. You can also right-click the video and choose Add Note. If you aren't connected, the extension asks you to connect before opening the editor. A note written at 12:40 in a lecture stays tied to 12:40, so you know which part of the video it belongs to. Notes are private: they are not posted to the site as comments. To read and edit notes, choose Notes from Your library on the widget's Tools tab. It opens your account's Notes page on the website.

In the same section, click the format you want. The export includes your account's notes and notes still waiting to sync from this browser. Button What you get Notes MD A Markdown file Notes TXT A text file Notes JSON A JSON file The Markdown export puts each note on its own line with its timestamp, so the file sits beside the rest of your lecture notes as it is.

Click Bookmark on the Tools tab, right-click the video and choose Add Bookmark, or press Ctrl + Alt + O. You can save a bookmark without an account; it stays in this browser. When the extension is connected, a new bookmark saves at the current moment and syncs to your account. Choose Bookmarks from Your library on the widget's Tools tab, or open the Bookmarks tab on the website's Notes page, to search, edit, delete or export account bookmarks. Bookmarks made before you connected remain only in that browser; connecting later does not upload them automatically. The Enable Cloud Sync switch controls settings sync separately.
Click Transcript in the same section to download the transcript as text. You read it outside the player.
Press Ctrl + Alt + X to copy a link to the video with the current timestamp, and it works on YouTube, Vimeo, Twitch and other sites. The link carries the time and nothing else.

Key What it does Ctrl + Alt + O Add a bookmark at the current moment Ctrl + Alt + X Copy a link with the timestamp Ctrl + Alt + C Capture the current frame Starting keys are in Default shortcuts, and Change a shortcut moves them. Next: Picture-in-Picture.
Press Ctrl + Alt + P to put the video in a Picture-in-Picture window, and press it again to bring it back. It works without an account.

Start the video. Press Ctrl + Alt + P. Switch to another tab. The video keeps playing in its own small window. Press Ctrl + Alt + P again to leave Picture-in-Picture. The keys stay with it: ] and [ change the speed of the small window too, and the rest of the speed controls keep working while it is in Picture-in-Picture.

On a long page the video scrolls out of view when you read the text under it. The extension can move it into Picture-in-Picture on its own when that happens. Open Settings and go to the Advanced tab. Find Playback Features. Make sure Picture-in-Picture is on. Turn on Auto-enter PiP on Scroll.
documents.s: Enter on its own when you scroll

documents.t: Key What it does Ctrl + Alt + P Picture-in-Picture on or off Ctrl + Alt + Z Theater mode on or off ] / [ 0.1x faster or slower, in the small window too To move any of them, start from Default shortcuts and follow Change a shortcut. Auto-skip comes next.

Automation blocks autoplay, keeps a speed for each site, ramps the speed up slowly and reminds you to watch a video later. Open the widget's Playback tab and find Automation. None of it needs an account. Settings, Video Features tab, Playback automation lists your blocked and allowed sites, your site speeds and your reminders, with Remove beside each one.
documents.s: Let playback run on its own with Automation

documents.t: Press Block autoplay here and videos on this site wait until you press play. A held video shows "Autoplay blocked — press play to watch". To block it on every site, turn on Block autoplay everywhere in Settings and add the sites you want to keep under Sites where autoplay is allowed. Tick Tell me when a blocked video is ready for a notice when a held video in a hidden tab is ready to play.

Set the speed you like, then press Keep 1.5x on this site (the button shows your current speed). Videos on that site now start at it. A speed the extension remembers for one video or one playlist still wins.
documents.s: Keep a speed for a site

documents.t: A speed ramp raises the speed bit by bit while the video plays. Pick where it ends, from 1.25x to 2.5x, and how long it takes, from 5 to 30 minutes, then press Start. It moves in 0.1x steps. Press Stop to end it.

Press Remind me to watch this and pick In 1 hour, Tonight 20:00, Tomorrow 08:00 or Pick a date and time…, then Repeat it Once, Daily or Weekly, and press Set. A browser notification arrives at that time. Click it to open the video. On YouTube it opens at the moment you saved. You can have up to 50 reminders at a time.

In Settings, Video Features tab, turn on Pause videos in other tabs when one starts. When a video starts, videos playing in your other tabs of this browser pause. It is off until you turn it on, and it needs no account.

This one needs a connected account. It starts off. In Settings, Video Features tab, turn on Play my Watch Later in order and pick a Countdown of 5, 10 or 15 seconds. When a video ends, a card over it counts down to the next video in your Watch Later list, or to the first one when the video you finished is not in the list, with Play now and Cancel. After the last video, nothing plays. Replaying or seeking back cancels it, and a looping video never ends, so it never moves on.

With Remember Playback Position on, a connected account and Watch History turned on, the extension can pick up where another device stopped. It asks: "You got to 12:40 on another device. Resume?" It does this only when this browser has no saved position of its own, and not near the very end of the video.
"Block autoplay on this site" and "Start or stop the speed ramp" start with no key. Give them one in Change a shortcut. Next: Watch limits and Focus Mode.
Press Ctrl + Alt + C to save the current frame as PNG or JPEG; it needs an account.
documents.s: Take a screenshot of a video frame

documents.t: Pause on the frame you want, or leave the video playing. Press Ctrl + Alt + C, or click Capture on the widget's Tools tab. The frame is downloaded, copied or uploaded, depending on the action you chose in Settings. Pause, press , or . to step one frame at a time, and you capture the exact frame where the slide is complete.

Open Settings, go to the Video Features tab and find the Screenshot card. Option Choices Format PNG (higher quality) or JPEG (smaller file) Action Download, Copy to Clipboard, Download + Clipboard, Upload to Cloud, or Cloud + Clipboard Cloud Visibility Private or Public, for the cloud actions Sync to cloud library On or off Include Timestamp On or off Timestamp Position Top Left, Top Right, Bottom Left, Bottom Right The timestamp is the video time of the frame, written on the image. Turn it on for lecture slides and you know where each one came from.
documents.s: Choose the format and where the image goes

documents.t: Choosing a cloud action uploads the image. Otherwise the capture stays on your device.
A screenshot is one frame. For a moving section, the clip recorder records a part of the video and downloads it, and its switch is Clip Recording, in Settings on the Download & Capture tab.
documents.s: One frame or a moving part

documents.t: Key What it does Ctrl + Alt + C Capture the frame , Step back one frame . Step forward one frame All three can be moved: see Default shortcuts for the starting keys and Change a shortcut for the steps. Notes and bookmarks is the next page.

Share & watch together on the widget's Tools tab shares a link at the current moment and records a clip shaped for social posts. It also starts a watch party. Sharing a moment needs no account, while a social clip and a watch party need a connected account, and in a party every person who joins needs one.
documents.s: Share a moment and watch together

documents.t: Press Share this moment. The panel shows the link at the current time, the same link Ctrl + Alt + X copies. Copy link puts it on your clipboard. The QR code is made on your device. Save QR code saves it as a PNG. The buttons below send it to X, Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Reddit or Email.

Pick a Clip shape: Original, Square 1:1 or Vertical 9:16. Then press Clip for social. It records with the clip recorder, cropped to the center of the picture, and ■ Stop clip ends it. It does not work on protected video.

Open the video you want to watch together. Press Start a watch party. Press Copy invite link, or share the 10-character party code. A friend who gets the invite link sees a website page called "You are invited to watch together" and presses Open the video and join. A friend with the code opens the same video, types it under Party code and presses Join. While the party runs, the widget shows who is there and the code. Play, pause, a jump to a new time and the speed stay in step for everyone, up to 20 people. Leave takes you out. End the party is for the host, and a party also ends by itself after 6 hours. One person can have up to 3 parties running at a time. There is no chat. Use whatever you already talk in.

The live sync runs through Supabase Realtime and only the party's members receive it. The play, pause, jump and speed messages are not stored. The party itself keeps the video's address and title and the party code. It also keeps who joined and when. The privacy page has the details.
documents.s: What a party sends and keeps

documents.t: Message What it means "This watch party has ended or the code is not right." Check the code, or ask the host for a new one "This watch party is full (20 people)." The party has reached 20 people "You already have 3 watch parties running. End one first." End a party before you start another "Connect your account to use watch parties." Connect an account, then try again "A party code is 10 letters and numbers." The code you typed is the wrong length or has other characters Next: Default shortcuts.
Press ] or [ for 0.1x steps, or drag the slider in the widget up to 4x. The bracket keys work on their own, without Ctrl + Alt, and speed control works without an account.

Key What it does ] 0.1x faster [ 0.1x slower = Back to your default speed \ Show the current speed ' Sync to dynamic speed Ctrl + Alt + 1 0.5x Ctrl + Alt + 2 1x Ctrl + Alt + 3 1.5x Ctrl + Alt + 4 2x Ctrl + Alt + 5 2.5x Ctrl + Alt + 6 3x Ctrl + Alt + 7 3.5x Ctrl + Alt + 8 4x

The range is 0.1x to 16x. The slider and the bracket keys stop at 4x. Type a speed into the custom input on the widget's Speed tab, or into the Custom Speed (0.1x - 16x) boxes on the General tab in Settings, and the video plays at up to 16x. The step is always 0.1x. Settings has no control for the minimum speed, the maximum speed or the step.

Open Settings and go to the General tab. Setting What it is Key Default Playback Speed The speed used when you reset and when a new video loads = Current Dynamic Speed A second speed you set here and apply with one key ' The ' key applies the Current Dynamic Speed. It is not the speed saved for the video.
documents.s: Your default speed and the dynamic speed

documents.t: There are 8 presets on Ctrl + Alt + 1 to Ctrl + Alt + 8. Each one can be edited, and you can remove the ones you don't use. You do that in Settings, on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab. Add a ninth preset to use Ctrl + Alt + 9.

The extension remembers the speed you set for a video, and it applies it the next time you open that video. That is on by default. It can also remember one speed for a whole playlist or course; that switch is off by default, and you turn it on in Settings on the Advanced tab. When a video has more than one saved speed, Speed Priority decides which one wins: Setting Which speed wins Playlist/Course first The speed saved for the playlist or course Video first The speed saved for the video Global only (ignore saved) Your default speed, and saved speeds are ignored
, and . step back and forward one frame. The whole set is in Default shortcuts, and Change a shortcut shows how to move one. The next control is the A-B loop.

From the widget's Tools tab you can save a quiz at the current moment, a word with its caption line, a diary entry, and the video itself to a learning path or a collection. Each one needs a connected account and is kept in your account, with the video's title and address. Signed out, each section shows how to connect instead.
documents.s: Save quizzes, words, diary entries and videos to your library

documents.t: Under Quiz at this moment, write a Question and its Answer, then press Save quiz. It is saved as a flashcard. When you play past that moment in the same video, the video pauses and the question appears. Press Show answer, then I knew it or Not yet, which grade the card the same way the Flashcards page does. No quizzes on this video turns them off for this visit. Each moment asks once per visit, and seeking past it does not ask.

Type one Word under Save a word and press Look up. Up to three meanings appear. Press Save word, and it is saved as a flashcard with the caption line on screen as its example. The word is looked up at Wiktionary. Only the word is sent.

Pick a Mood (Happy, Inspired, Calm, Thoughtful, Sad or Frustrated), write What this moment meant to you, and press Save to diary. The entry is a bookmark in the folder "Diary", tagged with the mood, so you can edit it in Bookmarks too.

Under Learning path or Collection, pick one of yours and press Add this video. A video that is already there is refused. Make paths and collections on the website first; until you do, the widget says there are none yet. A learning-path video is marked done by itself once Watch History shows you watched it, which means you got past 90% of the video and played at least half of it along the way. Skipping to the end does not count. Watch History is off until you turn it on in Settings, on the Privacy & Data tab.

Search your library is in the widget's Your library menu and in the popup's library grid. It opens the website's search across your notes, bookmarks and diary entries, flashcards and saved words, transcripts, Watch Later, Watch History, collections and learning paths. Type 2 to 100 characters. You get up to 10 results for each kind, each with a link to its moment.

Page What it shows Flashcards Your quiz moments and saved words, to review Vocabulary Your saved words, each linking to its moment Clip Diary Your diary entries by day, newest first, with a mood filter Course Progress Each learning path's done and total, and the next video Collections Your collections, with a download as JSON, CSV, Markdown or an M3U playlist Next: Share and watch together.

The Study timer runs focus rounds and breaks, the transcript panel shows the captions a video already has beside it, and Make chapters with AI turns those captions into chapters. The timer and the transcript need no account.
documents.s: Study with a timer, a transcript and chapters

documents.t: Open the widget's Smart tab and find Study timer. Pick a Preset: Classic 25/5, Short 15/3, Long focus 50/10, Study 45/10, or Your own lengths. Press Start. The timer shows Focus, Break or Long break, and which round you are on. Press Pause and Resume as you need, or Skip to break. Reset the timer starts over. It counts today's focus minutes against your Daily focus goal and shows a day streak. One timer runs for the whole browser. Its counts stay in this browser. Settings, Video Features tab, Study timer sets the lengths, Long break after (rounds) and the goal. It can also Pause the video during breaks and Play it again when the break ends, with a Sound at the end of a round or a Browser notification at the end of a round.

Press Show transcript on the widget's Tools tab. The panel opens beside the widget with the captions the video already has, and the line playing now is highlighted. Click a line to jump there. Type in Search the transcript to find a line. Follow the video keeps the playing line in view. Copy all copies the whole transcript. It works on videos that carry captions. A video with none shows "This video has no captions, so there is no transcript." The extension does not make captions from the audio.

In the transcript panel, press Make chapters with AI. One AI run turns the captions into 3 to 15 chapters. It uses the same route as the AI summary: your Shared allowance with a connected account, your own key, or a local model (AI features). Click a chapter to jump to it. The playing chapter is marked. Copy chapters gives "0:00 Title" lines, and Make again spends a new run. Chapters are kept for each video in this browser, for up to 50 videos.

On the widget's Loop tab, Practice helps you learn a hard part of an A-B loop, which needs a connected account. Pause before each pass waits 1 to 5 seconds at point A. Speed up each pass adds 5% or 10% each time, up to normal speed. Set a slower speed first.
"Start or pause the study timer" and "Show or hide the transcript" start with no key. Set them in Change a shortcut. Next: Your library from the video.

The filters are brightness, contrast and saturation from 0% to 200%, plus grayscale, invert and night mode. With a connected account (what connecting adds), press Ctrl + Alt + F to open the Filters tab in the widget.
documents.s: Adjust the picture with video filters

documents.t: Control Range or effect Key Filters tab Opens and closes the Filters tab Ctrl + Alt + F Brightness 0% to 200% Slider Contrast 0% to 200% Slider Saturation 0% to 200% Slider Grayscale On or off Ctrl + Alt + G Invert On or off Ctrl + Alt + I Night mode On or off Ctrl + Alt + T 100% is the picture as the site sends it. Below 100% is less, above is more, and each slider stops at 200%. Reset All Filters on the same tab puts everything back.

A screen recording with pale gray text on white is hard to read. Raise the contrast. On a bright afternoon a dark video is hard to see. Raise the brightness. A whiteboard lecture late at night is a white rectangle in a dark room, so press Ctrl + Alt + I to invert it, or Ctrl + Alt + T for night mode.

Set the three sliders the way you want them and save the result as a preset on the Filters tab. You can save up to 20 presets, and since presets are part of your settings, they can be included when you export your settings.

Two other widget tabs change the picture, and neither one is the Filters tab. Where Control What it does View tab, Transform Rotate, mirror, flip Rotates the picture 90 degrees, mirrors it horizontally or flips it vertically Tools tab, Visual Modes Ambient Ambient light around the player Tools tab, Visual Modes Cinema A cinema color preset Tools tab, Visual Modes Letterbox Cinema bars above and below the picture Filters change how the video is drawn in your browser. A screenshot or a download is a separate control.
The filter keys sit in the full table in Default shortcuts, and Change a shortcut has the steps to move one. Next: Screenshots.

Looks & overlays adds color grades, art looks, sharpening, a vignette, film grain, a text overlay and blurred regions to the video. It sits on the widget's Filters tab, which needs a connected account, like the rest of that tab. Zoom & fit is on the View tab and needs no account. Every effect changes only the picture on the page, never the video file. Some streaming sites block effects on protected video, and the extension does not claim they work there.
documents.s: Add looks and effects, and zoom the picture

documents.t: Open the widget's Filters tab and find Looks & overlays. Control What it does Colour grade One of 20 grades, such as Teal & orange, Film noir, Vintage 8mm, Golden hour and Moonlight, with a Strength slider Art look Oil painting, Pencil sketch, Engraving or Coloured emboss Sharpen 0% to 100%, in steps of 10, applied before the color tools Vignette Darkens the corners of the picture Film grain Adds grain, still or moving Text Puts your Overlay text in a corner of the video Blur a region Drag a box on the video to blur that part Turn all effects off Puts the picture back A blurred region stays until you remove it with Remove blurred regions or the video changes. No video pixels are read. The blur happens on the page.

Settings, Video Features tab, Effects holds the finer options: Vignette strength, Grain strength, Moving grain, Overlay text and Text corner (Top left, Top right, Bottom left or Bottom right). Reset effects returns them to their defaults. Effects work with Video filters and the Comfort tools at the same time, and they follow the video into fullscreen.

Open the widget's View tab and find Zoom & fit. No account needed. Press Zoom in or Zoom out. The zoom goes from 1x to 4x in quarter steps, and pinching on a trackpad works too. Use the four arrows to move the view left, up, down or right. Turn on Magnifier: follow the pointer and the zoomed part follows your mouse. Pick a Fit: Original, Fill (crop the bars), Stretch, 4:3, 16:9 or 21:9. Back to the original picture resets it. Zoom works with rotate, mirror and flip, and Reset Transform leaves the zoom where it is. A new video starts at Original, and nothing here is stored.
Two optional shortcuts start with no key: "Turn effects on or off" and "Blur a region of the video". Both need a connected account when pressed. Set them in Change a shortcut. Next: Audio tools.

Watch limits set how much video you watch in a day, on all sites or on one site, and block sites where videos should not play. Focus Mode darkens the page around the video and hides what pulls your eyes away. Both are on the Video Features tab in Settings. Neither needs an account.
documents.s: Set watch limits and use Focus Mode

documents.t: Open Settings, go to the Video Features tab and find Watch limits. Turn on Watch limits. Set Daily limit, all sites, from 30 minutes to 4 hours. Pick Warn me before a limit: 5, 10 or 15 minutes before. Under Site limits, type a Site and its Minutes a day, then press Add. Under Blocked sites, add a site where videos do not play at all. The card shows Today on this device with the minutes so far.

The video pauses under a layer that says "Your watching time for today is up", or "Your time on this site is up for today" for a site limit. Press 5 more minutes to keep going a little, or Close. The count starts again at midnight. On a blocked site the layer says "Videos on this site are blocked".

Set a New PIN of 4 to 8 digits and type it again under PIN again. Press Lock. Changing limits, unblocking a site or taking 5 more minutes then asks for it. Remove the PIN takes it off. Keep the PIN somewhere safe. It is hashed and stays on this device, and it is never synced.

Minutes are counted on this device only, and only while limits are on, and the extension keeps nothing but today's minutes for each site, which start again at midnight. Nothing is sent. Watch limits help keep habits, or a child's watching, on track. They are not tamper-proof: someone who can change the browser's extension data can get around them. Getting started Install Video Controls Plus Add Video Controls Plus from the Chrome Web Store, Microsoft Edge Add-ons or Firefox Add-ons, and speed control works as soon as it is installed. Your first video with Video Controls Plus Open a video, change the speed with the bracket keys, find the widget and the popup, and see which controls need a connected account. User guide Control the playback speed Change video speed in 0.1x steps with the bracket keys or the widget slider up to 4x, type a custom speed up to 16x, and use 8 preset speeds. Loop a part of a video with an A-B loop Set point A and point B and the video replays the stretch between them, forever, once, or 1 to 20 times; the A-B loop needs an account. Boost the audio past 100% Raise a video's volume up to 400% and switch on normalize to even out loud and quiet parts; audio boost needs an account. Adjust the picture with video filters With a connected account, set brightness, contrast and saturation from 0% to 200%, use grayscale, invert or night mode, and save up to 20 presets. Make videos easier on your eyes with Comfort Warm the picture, make colors easier to tell apart, restyle a site's own captions and add a reading guide; Comfort needs no account and sends nothing. Add looks and effects, and zoom the picture With a connected account, add 20 color grades, four art looks, sharpen, vignette, film grain, a text overlay and blurred regions; Zoom & fit needs no account. Change the balance, voice, room and loudness With a connected account, set the left-right balance, change a voice without changing the speed, add a room, even out loudness and set a limiter; not on protected video. Make GIFs, clips, time-lapses and contact sheets With a connected account, make a GIF, record a clip or a time-lapse, take a screenshot burst, build a contact sheet and annotate a screenshot, all made on your device. Let playback run on its own with Automation Block autoplay, keep a speed per site, ramp the speed up, set reminders and pause other tabs, with no account; Up next and resume from another device need a connected account. Set watch limits and use Focus Mode Set a daily amount of video, limits for single sites and blocked sites, lock them with a PIN, and choose what Focus Mode hides; no account, and nothing is sent. Study with a timer, a transcript and chapters Run focus rounds and breaks with the Study timer, read a video's own captions as a transcript, turn them into chapters with one AI run, and practice a loop. Save quizzes, words, diary entries and videos to your library With a connected account, save a quiz moment, a word, a diary entry, a learning-path video or a collection item from the widget, and search everything you saved. Share a moment and watch together Share a link at the current time with a QR code, record a square or vertical clip, and start a watch party for up to 20 people that keeps play, pause, seeking and speed in step. Take a screenshot of a video frame Press Ctrl + Alt + C to save the current video frame as PNG or JPEG, download it or copy it, with an optional timestamp; it needs an account. Take notes and add bookmarks while you watch Save notes with the video timestamp from the widget's Tools tab, export them as Markdown, text or JSON, and add a bookmark at the current moment. Watch in Picture-in-Picture Press Ctrl + Alt + P to put the video in a Picture-in-Picture window, or let it enter on its own when you scroll away; it works without an account. Skip intros, recaps and credits automatically Auto-skip clicks the skip buttons that Netflix, Prime Video and YouTube show; it is off by default and needs an account. Choose how the controls appear on the page Pick the floating widget or notification only, set the widget's position, size and how it opens, and choose a theme and a language. Keyboard shortcuts Default keyboard shortcuts Every default key in Video Controls Plus: letter and digit keys need Ctrl + Alt, only the bracket, punctuation and Esc keys work alone, and the optional shortcuts start with no key. Change a keyboard shortcut Give any shortcut another key in Settings, switch shortcuts off one by one or by section, and keep your keys across devices with a connected account. Platforms Video Controls Plus on YouTube On YouTube the core controls work as on any site, and each of the YouTube extras has its own switch in Settings; most are on by default. Video Controls Plus on Netflix Speed and the core controls work on Netflix; the Netflix extras are off until you switch them on, and recovery keys take over in one case. Video Controls Plus on LinkedIn On LinkedIn the core video controls work, and a set of LinkedIn tools run from the widget or the right-click menu; switches are in Settings. Which sites Video Controls Plus works on Video Controls Plus works on any site that plays a standard HTML5 video, including embedded players, with extra tools on YouTube, Netflix and LinkedIn.
